originalTitle: Madhusudan Kela’s portfolio: 7 stocks rally up to 135% in CY26
simplifiedContent: Madhusudan Kela is an investor who has a portfolio of 19 stocks worth around Rs 2,665 crore. Some of the stocks in his portfolio have done very well, with 7 of them going up in value by 10-135% this year. On the other hand, 5 of his stocks have lost value, going down by 15-30%. This shows that his investments have had very different results, with some doing very well and others not as well. This matters because it gives an idea of how his investment choices are performing, and can be useful for other investors to consider when making their own decisions.

originalTitle: Bitcoin near $63,000 as weaker ETF demand and cancelled SEC meeting dampen crypto sentiment
simplifiedContent: The price of Bitcoin is currently around $63,000. This is because people are not buying as many Bitcoin-related investment funds (called ETFs) as before, and a meeting with the US securities regulator (the SEC) was cancelled. As a result, people are feeling less positive about investing in cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum, which has caused their prices to go down. The total value of all cryptocurrencies has decreased by 0.4%, showing a slight decline in the market. This change in sentiment may be due to uncertainty about what rules and regulations will apply to cryptocurrencies.

originalTitle: F&O Talk: Nifty consolidation to continue says Sudeep Shah; gives Tata Motors, Lenskart, Honasa strategy
simplifiedContent: The stock market, specifically the Nifty, is currently not moving much and is expected to stay that way for a while. This means that the Nifty's value will likely stay between 24,150 and 24,600. The fact that volatility is falling suggests that there won't be any big surprises, and options data indicates that the market doesn't expect the Nifty to go down much further. Analysts are currently favoring certain types of stocks, including those from PSU banks, defence, auto, and chemicals, which they think are strong. This information can help investors make informed decisions about where to put their money.

originalTitle: Independence Day 2026:  ₹89 to  ₹1,54,500 — gold price rises 1,73,500% in 79 years; here's how
simplifiedContent: The price of gold has increased significantly over the past 79 years. In 1947, when India became independent, the price of gold was around ₹89 for 10 grams. Today, the price of gold is approximately ₹1,54,500 for the same amount, which is a huge increase of 1,73,500%. This means that if you had bought gold in 1947, its value would have risen greatly over time. This large price increase is notable and shows how the value of gold has changed dramatically since India's independence.

originalTitle: IPO GMPs: Milky Mist IPO to Behari Lal Engineering IPO - what grey market hints
simplifiedContent: There are some new companies that are planning to sell their shares to the public for the first time, which is called an Initial Public Offering (IPO). Two of these companies, Dhoot Transmission and Molbio Diagnostics, are going to start selling their shares on August 17. Many investors are interested in buying these shares, and the prices that people are willing to pay for them before they are officially available (known as the grey market) are higher than expected. This suggests that investors are optimistic about these companies and think their shares will do well when they start trading. As a result, it's likely that the shares will start trading at a higher price than their initial sale price.

originalTitle: Buy or sell: Sumeet Bagadia recommends these three Independence Day stock picks. Should you buy?
simplifiedContent: A finance expert named Sumeet Bagadia has suggested three stocks to consider investing in to celebrate India's Independence Day.
